historical_reviews.deepseek: The operator boundary is correct, but no particular SIO function can be exercised safely from a generic menu/port statement.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Classification and per-device/port controls are accepted; functional-port evidence is bound only to the selected option while persistence remains the direct Master criterion.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code searches found no duplicate variant; sequence 1705 covers the preceding controller-wide Common Setting and is not merged here.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Per-device SIO configuration must bind a named logical function to its physical header/connector and OS/firmware identity so a saved value is not verified against the wrong port.

original_test_intent: Have a qualified operator demonstrate save/re-entry persistence for one explicitly approved per-device SIO Configuration option and, where specified, verify the corresponding physical-port function on the mapped connector.
original_method: Bind the SIO controller, logical device and physical port; capture baseline BIOS value and port state; change only the named device option to the approved value, save/reboot/re-enter, verify persistence and specified port behavior, then restore and verify baseline.
manual_activity: The owner selects the exact SIO device option and port/function contract; a qualified operator handles BIOS, fixture/port observation, reboot and restoration.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/board, BIOS and SIO controller/device identity
Exact SIO Configuration field and menu path
Logical device to physical connector/header mapping
Expected physical-port function and fixture, if required
safety_requirements: Never authorize arbitrary SIO setting changes
Change only the named per-device option
Keep Common Setting row coverage separate
Verify physical connector mapping before attaching or interpreting a fixture
Do not clear dmesg, syslog or SEL
Stop on unexpected device/port, IRQ/resource, boot or recovery behavior
No automatic retry or Load Defaults substitute
agent_execution_scope: Coordinate but do not claim BIOS or physical fixture control
Correlate only the approved mapped port behavior
Track final state and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Name device/field/values, port map, fixture, function and rollback
Perform or supervise UI and physical-port steps
Resolve resource/port anomalies and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its NO/manual result fits, but the generic physical-port instruction cannot execute without a named device, field, mapping and expected function.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Manual operator: capture the mapped SIO device field and port baseline, change only the approved value, save/reboot/re-enter, prove persistence, verify the specified connector function and restore baseline.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: SIO Configuration scope, setting persistence and 5/5-minute estimates remain; missing device/field/port values become required inputs and log clearing is prohibited.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record controller/device identity, logical-to-physical port map, exact field, baseline/test/restore values, before/save/re-entry captures and optional fixture result as one evidence tuple.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces arbitrary mutation with one mapped device checkpoint and distinguishes it from controller-wide common settings.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A successful selected option does not validate every SIO device; only owner-enumerated field and mapped-port coverage is claimed.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Incorrect SIO resource or port settings may disable console/legacy I/O, cause resource conflicts or impair boot/recovery.

project_override_considerations: Automated fixture capture can supplement evidence only after the physical mapping is owner-approved. Controller-wide Common Setting behavior remains covered by the preceding row, not this per-device configuration case.
expected_evidence: Logical device-to-physical port mapping and fixture identity
Exact field matrix and before/change/save/re-entry/restore BIOS captures
Persistence comparison and approved port-function result, if specified
Recovery/final state and engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require SIO Configuration persistence. Exact device/field/port semantics are missing readiness inputs rather than contradictory source requirements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The manual case is safely defined once the owner supplies a reversible device option, physical mapping, optional function oracle and recovery path.

review_improvement: Binds the BIOS write to one SIO device and mapped connector, prevents arbitrary mutation and separates per-device evidence from the preceding common-setting case.
independent_technical_reasoning: A per-device SIO option is only attributable when the BIOS logical device and physical connector are mapped. Otherwise persistence may be real but the observed port can belong to another UART/GPIO function, producing a false functional correlation.
